components.name: Action/AtlButton
components.description:
Action button. Maps to AtlButtonSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a user-initiated action — submit, save, delete, navigate. Pick the visual based on hierarchy: `primary` for the screen's main action (one per screen), `secondary` for supporting actions, `outline` for tertiary/inline, `danger` for destructive actions (delete, irreversible).

Don't use when: the action is a navigation link (use a real `<a>` element, not a styled button), the choice is between two states (use Form/AtlToggle), or the user is filling a form field (use Form/AtlInput / Form/AtlSelect).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `variant`: primary | secondary | outline | danger — maps to AtlButtonSpec.variant
- Variant `size`: sm | md | lg — maps to AtlButtonSpec.size
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus | active — interaction state
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlButtonSpec.disabled
- Boolean `loading`: maps to AtlButtonSpec.loading — shows spinner, disables interaction
- Boolean `hasIcon`: toggles the leading icon slot (Instance Swap → Icon library)

A11y: native HTML <button>. When the button has no visible label (icon-only), supply `aria-label` — required by spec. Disabled state uses HTML `disabled` (not aria-disabled) for buttons since they're never expected to remain in the tab order.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — `state` enum slimmed to interaction (default/hover/focus/active); `loading` and `disabled` moved out as Booleans matching AtlButtonSpec; `hasIcon` Boolean added for icon-slot toggle.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `hasIcon`: declared but unbound — and it maps to nothing: `AtlButtonSpec` has no `hasIcon`. It is a Figma-side slot toggle for placing an Icon instance, which is a legitimate authoring affordance but not part of the component contract. Bind it to the icon slot layer when that slot exists, or drop it.

components.name: Form/AtlInput
components.description:
Single-line text input. Maps to AtlInputSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a user needs to enter a short string (text, email, password, number, tel, url). For multi-line use Form/AtlTextarea. For options use Form/AtlSelect or Form/AtlCombobox.

Don't use when: input is binary (use Form/AtlCheckbox or Form/AtlToggle), the value is one-of-many (use Form/AtlRadioGroup), or the user is choosing from a set (use Form/AtlSelect).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus | invalid | filled — interaction + form state
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Boolean `readonly`: maps to AtlReadonlySpec.readonly
- Boolean `required`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.required
- (code-only props on AtlInputSpec: `type`, `placeholder`, `value`, `onValueChange`, `name`)

A11y: native HTML <input>; ARIA roles and keyboard come from the browser. Disabled state uses aria-disabled (not HTML disabled) so screen readers still announce it — pair with a tooltip/helper text explaining why. The invalid state is carried by an AtlIcon `danger` inside the field as well as by the border colour, so it does not depend on colour perception (WCAG 1.4.1); the error message is a polite live region the field points at with aria-describedby.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — old `state` enum (default/filled/focus/invalid/disabled/hover/active/loading) replaced by interaction Variant + orthogonal Booleans matching libs/spec. 2026-08-27 — `readonly` re-pointed from AtlFormFieldSpec to AtlReadonlySpec, where ADR-0045 moved it; the old mapping was caught by check:figma's [BOOL-CLAIM].

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `required`: declared but unbound — `required` renders nothing in any of the five form fields. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and that is all: no class, no CSS rule, no asterisk. The asterisk a designer expects comes from the label text the consumer writes, so there is no component-owned layer for this property to toggle. If the library should render one, that is a code change first.

components.name: Display/AtlCard
components.description:
Container for grouped content. Maps to AtlCardSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: distinct grouped content needs a visual container — list items, summaries, dashboard tiles. For overlay content use Overlay/AtlDialog or Overlay/AtlDrawer.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: elevated | outlined | flat → AtlCardSpec.variant
- Variant `padding`: none | sm | md | lg → AtlCardSpec.padding
- Text `Title`, `Body`: content slots
- (code-only: `role` — landmark role, default plain div)

A11y: defaults to <div>. Set `role` only when the card is meaningful as a landmark (article, region) — adding a landmark for every card pollutes the page outline.

components.name: Display/AtlBadge
components.description:
Inline status pill. Maps to AtlBadgeSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a small label needs to convey status, count, or category alongside other content. For larger callouts use Feedback/AtlAlert.

Don't use when: the content is a control (use Action/AtlButton) or it's the primary content of the screen.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: default | success | warning | danger | info → AtlBadgeSpec.variant
- Variant `size`: sm | md → AtlBadgeSpec.size
- Text `Label`: REMOVED 2026-08-27 (ADR-0067). AtlBadgeSpec has no label field — the text is children, and text inside a Figma instance is editable without a property, so the property added nothing but the implication of a prop that does not exist.

A11y: badges are decorative by default. If they convey state changes important to assistive tech, wrap in role="status".

components.name: Form/AtlSelect
components.description:
Dropdown selector. Maps to AtlSelectSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user picks one value from a fixed list of <50 options. For searchable lists use Form/AtlCombobox. For 2–7 visible options use Form/AtlRadioGroup. For multi-select use a Combobox or stacked Form/AtlCheckbox.

Don't use when: options are dynamic / fetched (use Form/AtlCombobox), the choice is binary (use Form/AtlToggle), or users benefit from seeing all options simultaneously (use Form/AtlRadioGroup).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus | open | filled
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Boolean `invalid`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.invalid
- Boolean `required`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.required
- Text `placeholder`: maps to AtlSelectSpec.placeholder

A11y: native popover via the HTML Popover API. Keyboard: ArrowUp/Down navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes. Disabled state uses aria-disabled (not HTML disabled).

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — `state` enum slimmed to interaction + open + filled; disabled/invalid/required moved to Booleans matching spec.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `required`: declared but unbound — `required` renders nothing in any of the five form fields. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and that is all: no class, no CSS rule, no asterisk. The asterisk a designer expects comes from the label text the consumer writes, so there is no component-owned layer for this property to toggle. If the library should render one, that is a code change first.

components.name: Overlay/AtlDialog
components.description:
Modal dialog. Maps to AtlDialogSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user input is required before continuing (confirmation, form, error). For non-blocking notifications use Overlay/AtlToast; for side panels use Overlay/AtlDrawer.

API surface:
- Variant `size`: sm | md | lg | xl | full → AtlDialogSpec.size
- Text `Title`, `Message`, `ConfirmLabel`, `CancelLabel`: content slots
- (code-only: `open`, `closeOnBackdrop`, `onOpenChange`)

A11y: ARIA dialog pattern with focus trap. Esc closes; first focusable element receives focus on open.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled as Boolean properties (2026-08-27, ADR-0056). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated here rather than hidden in a list inside the gate:
- Boolean `open`: not modelled — false renders nothing. The dialog is a native `<dialog>` driven by `showModal()` / `close()`, so a closed one is not on the screen at all. Unlike AtlChat, whose popup variant keeps a visible bubble when closed.
- Boolean `closeOnBackdrop`: not modelled — behaviour only. It decides whether a click outside dismisses the dialog; no CSS rule and no rendered element reference it.

components.name: Navigation/AtlTabGroup
components.description:
Tabbed content switcher. Maps to AtlTabGroupSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: peer content panels share a context and user picks one to view. For sequential steps use Navigation/AtlStepper.

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `variant`: default | pills → AtlTabGroupSpec.variant
- Variant `selected`: 0 | 1 — illustrative selection state
- Variant `state`: default — interaction state (legacy mash-up removed)
- Boolean `disabled`: disables every contained Tab
- Boolean `loading`: shows tab-bar skeleton / panel spinner

A11y: ARIA tabs pattern. Arrow keys move selection inside the tablist; Tab moves out. aria-controls links each tab to its panel.

Status: 2026-04-27 — `state` Variant slimmed from {default,focus,hover,active,loading,disabled,error} to default-only; disabled/loading moved to Booleans matching the Form/* pattern.

Axis notes (2026-08-27, ADR-0056): `selected` was renamed to `selectedIndex`, which is the actual prop on AtlTabGroupSpec — check:figma reported the old name as [AXIS-NAME]. `selectedIndex` is a number, so an axis can only ever picture a sample of it; the two options here are two of its values, not its range. The single-value axis `state` was removed: an axis with one option carries no information and reads as API that does not vary.

components.name: Feedback/AtlAccordionGroup
components.description:
Collapsible content sections. Maps to AtlAccordionGroupSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: content is partitioned into sections that don't all need to be visible simultaneously (FAQ, settings groups). For peer content where one is always visible use Navigation/AtlTabGroup.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: default | bordered | separated → AtlAccordionGroupSpec.variant
- (code-only: `multi` — boolean for allowing multiple panels open)

A11y: ARIA accordion pattern. Each panel's heading wraps a button; aria-expanded reflects state.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled as Boolean properties (2026-08-27, ADR-0056). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated here rather than hidden in a list inside the gate:
- Boolean `multi`: not modelled — behaviour only. It guards how many items MAY be open; a group showing two open items looks the same whether `multi` allowed it or the user opened them one at a time. No CSS rule and no render condition reference it.

components.name: Navigation/AtlMenu
components.description:
Action menu. Maps to AtlMenuSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: secondary actions on an item, triggered by a control (button, more icon). For navigation use a sidebar or Navigation/AtlTabGroup.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: default | compact → AtlMenuSpec.variant

A11y: ARIA menu pattern with roving tabindex; arrow keys navigate, Enter/Space activates, Escape closes.

components.name: Overlay/AtlTooltip
components.description:
Floating context label. Maps to AtlTooltipSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: brief non-essential clarification on hover/focus (e.g. icon-only buttons, abbreviations).

Don't use when: information is essential (put it in the visible label) or content is a paragraph (use Overlay/AtlDialog or a popover).

API surface:
- Variant `position`: above | below | left | right → AtlTooltipSpec.atlTooltipPosition
- Text `atlTooltip`: maps to AtlTooltipSpec.atlTooltip — the property carries the spec's own name, odd as it reads, because that is the field a consumer sets
- (code-only: `disabled`, `showDelay`, `hideDelay`)

A11y: tooltip role, anchored via aria-describedby on the trigger. Mobile users have no hover, so don't put critical info here.

Axis note (2026-08-27): the axis is `position`, derived from the spec union `AtlTooltipPosition` the way every other master derives its axis name from its union — `AtlButtonVariant` gives `variant`. It was briefly renamed to `atlTooltipPosition`, the Angular directive-input field name, on a check that compared against the field instead of the union. check:figma's [NAME] rule caught the rename as a blocker; the check was corrected rather than the master (ADR-0056).

Spec flags deliberately not modelled as Boolean properties (2026-08-27, ADR-0056). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated here rather than hidden in a list inside the gate:
- Boolean `atlTooltipDisabled`: not modelled — renders nothing. `atl-tooltip.tsx` early-returns on it, so there is no disabled tooltip to draw — only the absence of one.

components.name: Feedback/AtlAlert
components.description:
Inline notification with intent. Maps to AtlAlertSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a persistent message conveys status that the user should see while continuing on the page (form errors, banner notices). For transient feedback use Overlay/AtlToast.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: info | success | warning | danger → AtlAlertSpec.variant
- Boolean `dismissible` → AtlAlertSpec.dismissible
- Text `Message`: REMOVED 2026-08-27 (ADR-0067). The alert body is children; AtlAlertSpec has only `variant` and `dismissible`.

A11y: role="alert" for danger/warning (interrupts assistive tech); role="status" otherwise.

Status: 2026-04-27 — `dismissible` moved from Variant axis (false/true) to Boolean Property matching spec.

components.name: Form/AtlCheckbox
components.description:
Boolean form control for opt-in selections. Maps to AtlCheckboxSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user opts in to one or more independent options (Accept terms, Subscribe to newsletter, parent rows in a tree). Indeterminate state represents a partially-selected parent of mixed children.

Don't use when: choice is mutually exclusive (use Form/AtlRadio + Form/AtlRadioGroup) or binary settings toggle (use Form/AtlToggle — feels more like a switch than a form input).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `selection`: unchecked | checked | indeterminate — maps to `checked` + `indeterminate` Booleans
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus — interaction state
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Boolean `invalid`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.invalid
- Boolean `required`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.required
- Text `Label`: REMOVED 2026-08-27 (ADR-0067). The label is content projection, not a prop; AtlCheckboxSpec has no such field.

A11y: native HTML <input type="checkbox">. Indeterminate set via JS property (not HTML attribute). Disabled state uses aria-disabled.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — single `state` enum split into orthogonal `selection` (unchecked/checked/indeterminate) + `state` (default/hover/focus) Variant Properties; disabled moved to Boolean.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `required`: declared but unbound — `required` renders nothing in any of the five form fields. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and that is all: no class, no CSS rule, no asterisk. The asterisk a designer expects comes from the label text the consumer writes, so there is no component-owned layer for this property to toggle. If the library should render one, that is a code change first.

components.name: Form/AtlToggle
components.description:
On/off switch control. Maps to AtlToggleSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a binary setting takes effect immediately (notifications on/off, dark mode, sync). Visually distinct from Checkbox — the switch metaphor implies "this changes a setting now", not "this opts into a form value on submit".

Don't use when: the binary is part of a form submission (use Form/AtlCheckbox), the setting requires a confirmation step (use Form/AtlCheckbox plus Action/AtlButton), or the choice is one-of-three (use Form/AtlRadioGroup).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `selection`: off | on — maps to AtlToggleSpec.checked (false/true)
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus — interaction state
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Text `Label`: REMOVED 2026-08-27 (ADR-0067). The label is content projection, not a prop; AtlToggleSpec has no such field.

A11y: native HTML <input type="checkbox"> with role="switch" wrapper. The label should describe the setting being toggled, not "Off/On". Disabled state uses aria-disabled.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — collapsed Cartesian (`disabled-off`/`disabled-on`) into orthogonal `selection` Variant + `disabled` Boolean. Old `state` enum (off/on/disabled-off/disabled-on/focus/hover/active/loading) replaced.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled (2026-08-27, ADR-0058):
- Boolean `required`: not modelled — `required` renders nothing in any Atelier form field. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and stops there.

components.name: Form/AtlTextarea
components.description:
Multi-line text input. Maps to AtlTextareaSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user enters a paragraph or block of text (comment, description, message body). For single-line use Form/AtlInput.

Don't use when: input is a small fixed-shape value (use Form/AtlInput) or a one-of-many choice (use Form/AtlSelect).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus | invalid | filled
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Boolean `readonly`: maps to AtlReadonlySpec.readonly
- Boolean `required`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.required
- Boolean `autoResize`: maps to AtlTextareaSpec.autoResize — grow to fit content
- Text `placeholder`: maps to AtlTextareaSpec.placeholder

A11y: native HTML <textarea>. Disabled state uses aria-disabled (not HTML disabled) so the element remains focusable and is announced by screen readers — pair with helper text or aria-describedby explaining why. The invalid state is carried by an AtlIcon `danger` inside the field as well as by the border colour, so it does not depend on colour perception (WCAG 1.4.1); the error message is a polite live region the field points at with aria-describedby.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — old `state` enum collapsed; orthogonal Booleans now match AtlFormFieldSpec. 2026-08-27 — `readonly` re-pointed from AtlFormFieldSpec to AtlReadonlySpec, where ADR-0045 moved it; the old mapping was caught by check:figma's [BOOL-CLAIM].

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `required`: declared but unbound — `required` renders nothing in any of the five form fields. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and that is all: no class, no CSS rule, no asterisk. The asterisk a designer expects comes from the label text the consumer writes, so there is no component-owned layer for this property to toggle. If the library should render one, that is a code change first.
- Boolean `autoResize`: declared but unbound — `.is-auto-resize textarea` sets `resize: none; overflow: hidden`, which removes the browser's resize grabber. That grabber is chrome Figma does not draw in the first place, so there is no difference here to toggle.

components.name: Form/AtlRadioGroup
components.description:
Mutually exclusive option selector. Maps to AtlRadioGroupSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user picks exactly one of 2–7 visible options where seeing every option is valuable. Wrap Form/AtlRadio children inside the group — the group manages keyboard navigation (arrow keys move selection) and value binding.

Don't use when: option count exceeds ~7 (use Form/AtlSelect or Form/AtlCombobox), choices are independent (use Form/AtlCheckbox), or the choice is binary (use Form/AtlToggle).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `selection`: unselected | selected — group-level selection state for the gallery
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus — interaction state
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled — disables every contained Radio
- (code-only: `value: string` — the selected radio's `radioValue`)

A11y: ARIA radiogroup pattern with roving tabindex. Arrow keys move selection inside the group. Wrap in a fieldset + legend if the group has a visible label.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — single `state` enum split into orthogonal `selection` (unselected/selected) + `state` (default/hover/focus); disabled moved to Boolean.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled (2026-08-27, ADR-0058):
- Boolean `required`: not modelled — `required` renders nothing in any Atelier form field. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and stops there: no class, no CSS rule, no mark.
- Boolean `readonly`: not modelled — the component emits an `is-readonly` class and NO stylesheet in any of the three frameworks has a rule for it, so nothing renders differently. That dead class is the same shape ADR-0045 removed from AtlSelect and is recorded as a code finding.

components.name: Form/AtlRadio
components.description:
Individual radio button. Maps to AtlRadioSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a single option among a mutually-exclusive set. Always wrap in Form/AtlRadioGroup — the group manages keyboard navigation, focus, and value binding.

Don't use when: option is independent (use Form/AtlCheckbox), the choice is binary (use Form/AtlToggle), or the option set is long enough to need search (use Form/AtlCombobox).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `selection`: unchecked | checked
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlRadioSpec.disabled
- Boolean `invalid`: inherited from AtlRadioGroupSpec.invalid — not a prop on this component
- (code-only: `radioValue: string`)

A11y: native HTML <input type="radio"> participating in a roving-tabindex group via the parent AtlRadioGroup.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — single `state` enum split into orthogonal `selection` (unchecked/checked) + `state` (default/hover/focus); disabled/invalid moved to Booleans. 2026-08-27 — the `invalid` Boolean removed, property and prose both, per ADR-0056.

Why `invalid` is here although AtlRadioSpec does not declare it: the radio reads it from the group. `atl-radio.tsx` computes its class list with `ctx.invalid && 'is-invalid'`, and `atl-radio.css` has three `.atl-radio.is-invalid` rules, so an invalid radio is a real rendered state — it is just owned by AtlRadioGroup rather than by this component. The Boolean drives the `_invalid-border` overlay.

This property was deleted on 2026-08-27 and restored the same day: check:figma reported the old mapping to `AtlFormFieldSpec.invalid` as [BOOL-CLAIM], correctly — AtlRadioSpec extends nothing — and deleting the property was the wrong repair, because it orphaned the overlay layer that draws the state. The mapping was wrong; the property was not (ADR-0058).

components.name: Display/AtlSkeleton
components.description:
Loading placeholder. Maps to AtlSkeletonSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: content is being fetched and a layout-stable placeholder prevents layout shift on load.

Don't use when: load is <300ms (no perceived benefit) or the loading state is decorative — use Display/AtlProgress.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: text | circular | rectangular → AtlSkeletonSpec.variant
- (code-only: `width`, `height`, `animated`)

A11y: hidden from screen readers via aria-hidden — assistive tech announces the loading state via the parent region's aria-busy.

components.name: Display/AtlProgress
components.description:
Linear progress indicator. Maps to AtlProgressSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: an ongoing operation has known or unknown duration. Determinate (with value) shows progress; indeterminate just signals activity.

Don't use when: state isn't quantifiable nor ongoing — use Display/AtlSkeleton or a transient Overlay/AtlToast.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: default | success | warning | danger → AtlProgressSpec.variant
- Variant `size`: sm | md | lg → AtlProgressSpec.size
- Boolean `indeterminate` → AtlProgressSpec.indeterminate
- (code-only: `value`, `max`, `label` — required aria-label for screen readers)

A11y: `label` prop is required by ARIA when no visible label is nearby; otherwise screen readers announce only "progress bar 47%".

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058):
- Boolean `indeterminate`: declared but unbound — the state REPLACES the fill rather than adding a layer. `.atl-progress.is-indeterminate .fill` sets `width: 40% !important` and animates it, so the determinate fill must go away at the same moment the indeterminate one appears. A Figma Boolean toggles one layer on; it cannot toggle another off, so a second fill bound to this property would show both bars at once. This belongs on a variant axis — the shape ADR-0058 records for a replacing state, as against an adding one (a Boolean) or a colour-changing one (an overlay, like `_invalid-border`).

components.name: Display/AtlAvatar
components.description:
Avatar with graceful image → initials → icon fallback. Maps to AtlAvatarSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: representing a user or entity. For multiple stacked avatars, use AtlAvatarGroup (deferred — currently illustrated by sibling frames in this section).

API surface:
- Variant `shape`: circle | square → AtlAvatarSpec.shape
- Variant `size`: xs | sm | md | lg | xl → AtlAvatarSpec.size
- Text `Initials`: REMOVED 2026-08-27 (ADR-0067). The initials are DERIVED, not set: `atl-avatar.tsx` computes `getInitials(name)` from AtlAvatarSpec.name. A property offering to set them would let a designer type something the component can never render.
- (code-only: `src`, `alt`, `name`, `status`)

Status: spec field `status` (online/offline/away/busy) is illustrated alongside but not yet a Variant axis — follow-up.

components.name: Overlay/AtlToast
components.description:
Transient notification. Maps to AtlToastVariant + AtlToastOptions + AtlToastContainerPosition in libs/spec.

Use when: non-blocking feedback for an async action (saved, copied, error). For critical interruptions use Overlay/AtlDialog.

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `variant`: default | success | warning | danger | info → AtlToastVariant
- Variant `position`: top-right | top-center | bottom-right | bottom-center → AtlToastContainerPosition (where the toast container anchors on the page)
- Boolean `dismissible` → AtlToastOptions.dismissible
- Text `message`: not a property — the message is the FIRST ARGUMENT of the toast service call, and AtlToastOptions covers only the options object. AtlToast has no spec interface at all (allowlisted in check-figma).
- (code-only: `duration: number` → AtlToastOptions.duration)

A11y: aria-live="polite" for default/success/info; aria-live="assertive" for warning/danger.

Status: 2026-04-27 — `position` Variant axis added per AtlToastContainerPosition. Asymmetric matrix: 5 variants × top-right + 3 illustrative (default × top-center, bottom-right, bottom-center). Cross-product (5×4) can be filled later. `dismissible` Boolean added.

components.name: Navigation/AtlBreadcrumbs
components.description:
Hierarchical navigation trail. Maps to AtlBreadcrumbsSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: pages live in a hierarchy and the user benefits from seeing where they are. For top-level navigation use Navigation/AtlTabGroup or a sidebar.

API surface:
- Variant `items`: 3 | 4 | 5 — illustrative item-count Variants
- (code-only: `separator` string)

A11y: aria-label="Breadcrumb" on the nav element; current page marked aria-current="page".

Axis notes (2026-08-27, ADR-0056): this was a COMPONENT_SET whose only axis pictured an outcome of content rather than a property — `items` = 3 | 4 | 5, and AtlBreadcrumbsSpec is `{ separator?: string }`. An axis is the master's API surface, so a reader saw API where there was none. The other two drawings are kept as content samples in the "Content samples — not variant axes" section on this page. check:figma reported the axis as [AXIS-NOT-A-PROP].

components.name: Navigation/AtlPagination
components.description:
Page navigator for paged data. Maps to AtlPaginationSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: data spans many pages and user navigates incrementally. For infinite scroll surfaces, omit pagination entirely.

API surface:
- Variant `page`: first | middle | last — illustrative position
- (code-only: `page`, `pageCount`, `siblingCount`, `showFirstLast`)

A11y: nav with aria-label="Pagination"; current page marked aria-current="page".

Axis notes (2026-08-27, ADR-0056): this was a COMPONENT_SET whose only axis pictured an outcome of content rather than a property — `position` = first | middle | last, and AtlPaginationSpec is `{ page, pageCount, siblingCount, showFirstLast }`. An axis is the master's API surface, so a reader saw API where there was none. The other two drawings are kept as content samples in the "Content samples — not variant axes" section on this page. check:figma reported the axis as [AXIS-NOT-A-PROP].

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058):
- Boolean `showFirstLast`: declared but unbound — because THE MASTER HAS NO FIRST/LAST CONTROL to bind it to. It draws `‹ Prev`, the page numbers with two ellipses, and `Next ›`. `AtlPaginationSpec.showFirstLast` gates a separate pair of buttons that render `«` and `»` in the code (now the chevron-double-left / -right icons), and those buttons are simply not drawn here. I bound the first and last PAGE NUMBER buttons by mistake and reverted it: hiding page 1 and page 10 is not what the prop does. Draw the two controls, then bind.

Glyphs replaced 2026-08-27 (ADR-0058): the prev and next controls drew `‹ Prev` and `Next ›` — a pictogram as a character AND a visible word. Both buttons are icon-only in the code, named for assistive tech by `aria-label="Previous page"` / `"Next page"`, so the word was the master's invention. They are chevron-left and chevron-right instances now.

components.name: Overlay/AtlDrawer
components.description:
Side panel. Maps to AtlDrawerSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: content needs more room than a Tooltip but should not block the underlying view (filters, settings, multi-section content).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `position`: right | left | top | bottom → AtlDrawerSpec.position
- Variant `size`: sm | md | lg | full → AtlDrawerSpec.size
- Boolean `closeOnBackdrop` → AtlDrawerSpec.closeOnBackdrop
- (code-only: `open: boolean`)

A11y: ARIA dialog with focus trap; aria-labelledby names the drawer's heading. Esc closes. First focusable element receives focus on open.

Status: 2026-04-27 — `size` Variant filled out per spec. Asymmetric matrix: 4 positions on `md` + 3 sizes (sm/lg/full) on `right`. Cross-product (4×4) can be filled later by cloning.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled as Boolean properties (2026-08-27, ADR-0056). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated here rather than hidden in a list inside the gate:
- Boolean `open`: not modelled — false renders nothing — the same native `<dialog>` mechanism as AtlDialog.
- Boolean `closeOnBackdrop`: not modelled — behaviour only, as on AtlDialog.

components.name: Display/AtlTable
components.description:
Tabular data display. Maps to AtlTableSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: rows of comparable data need scanning by column. For lists of dissimilar items use Display/AtlCard stacks.

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `variant`: default | striped | bordered → AtlTableSpec.variant
- Variant `size`: sm | md | lg → AtlTableSpec.size
- Variant `state`: default — interaction state (legacy mash-up removed; specific states moved to Booleans)
- Boolean `sortable` → AtlTableSpec.sortable
- Boolean `selectable` → AtlTableSpec.selectable
- Boolean `stickyHeader` → AtlTableSpec.stickyHeader
- Boolean `disabled` → AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled (whole-table disabled)
- Boolean `loading` → row skeletons / spinner overlay
- Boolean `empty` → empty-state placeholder rendered instead of rows
- Boolean `error` → error banner / row replacement

A11y: aria-label required for screen-reader region announcement. Wrapper is keyboard-focusable (tabindex=0) for horizontal scroll.

Status: 2026-04-27 — `state` Variant slimmed from {default,empty,focus,hover,active,loading,disabled,error} to default-only; visual states moved to orthogonal Booleans matching AtlFormFieldSpec patterns used across Form/*.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `stickyHeader` is NOT exempt and is deliberately left reported: it is a real container prop (`AtlTableSpec.stickyHeader`) with a visual: `.atl-table.is-sticky-header thead th` adds `box-shadow: 0 1px 0 0 border`. It needs that shadow drawn as a layer and bound. Owed, not exempt.
- Boolean `sortable`: declared but unbound — it belongs to `AtlThSpec`, not `AtlTableSpec`. The container is carrying a child's state, which is why nothing could reference it. It moves to the AtlTh master when that exists (ADR-0056).
- Boolean `selectable`: declared but unbound — it belongs to `AtlTrSpec`. Same shape as `sortable`: a child's state on the container.
- Boolean `empty`: declared but unbound — it belongs to `AtlTbodySpec`. Same shape again.
- Boolean `error`: declared but unbound — and it maps to nothing at all. No table spec declares `error`, no CSS rule references it and no render condition uses it. Drop it, or decide what an errored table looks like and add the prop to the spec first.

components.name: Display/AtlCodeBlock
components.description:
Code snippet display. Not in libs/spec — UI helper component for rendering source code.

Use when: showing source code, command-line examples, or other technical content with monospace formatting.

API surface:
- Variant `variant`: default | with-filename | with-line-numbers | no-copy

A11y: <pre><code> with role="region" + aria-label naming the language.

components.name: Form/AtlCombobox
components.description:
Combobox — searchable select. Maps to AtlComboboxSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: user picks one value from a long or dynamic list (50+ options, fetched data, type-ahead). For short fixed lists use Form/AtlSelect.

Don't use when: list is short and known up-front (use Form/AtlSelect), or user must compare options side by side (use Form/AtlRadioGroup).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `state`: default | hover | focus | open | filtered | selected
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.disabled
- Boolean `invalid`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.invalid
- Boolean `required`: maps to AtlFormFieldSpec.required
- (code-only: `options: AtlComboboxOption[]`, `placeholder`)

A11y: combines a text input with a dropdown list. Arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Escape closes. Disabled state uses aria-disabled.

Status: structural restructure 2026-04-27 — `state` enum slimmed to interaction + open + filtered + selected; disabled/invalid/required moved to Booleans matching spec.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `required`: declared but unbound — `required` renders nothing in any of the five form fields. It is passed to the DOM as the HTML attribute and that is all: no class, no CSS rule, no asterisk. The asterisk a designer expects comes from the label text the consumer writes, so there is no component-owned layer for this property to toggle. If the library should render one, that is a code change first.

components.name: Navigation/AtlStepper
components.description:
Sequential progress through a multi-step flow. Maps to AtlStepperSpec + AtlStepSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a task is broken into clear sequential steps where progress matters (checkout, onboarding, multi-page form).

Don't use when: steps are independent (use Navigation/AtlTabGroup) or step count is dynamic.

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `orientation`: horizontal | vertical → AtlStepperSpec.orientation
- Variant `state`: default | completed | error | optional → maps to AtlStepSpec flags (completed/error/optional)
- Boolean `linear` → AtlStepperSpec.linear (when true, only the active and completed steps are clickable)
- (code-only: `activeStep: number`)

A11y: ol with aria-label naming the flow; current step aria-current="step". Each step's clickability reflects `linear` + completed state.

Status: 2026-04-27 — single `variant` axis (default|completed|error|optional|vertical) split into orthogonal `orientation` + `state` Variant Properties. Full 2×4 matrix populated (8 variants total). Vertical-state visual indicators (V/completed, V/error, V/optional) currently inherit V/default content as placeholder — designer polish deferred. Horizontal-state variants carry the canonical state visuals.

Spec flags deliberately not modelled as Boolean properties (2026-08-27, ADR-0056). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated here rather than hidden in a list inside the gate:
- Boolean `linear`: not modelled — behaviour only. `atl-stepper.tsx` uses it in one place — `if (linear && i > activeStep) return` — to refuse a jump ahead. Nothing about the drawing changes.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads these lines, so the reason is stated where a designer opening the master sees it:
- Boolean `linear`: declared but unbound — behaviour only. `atl-stepper.tsx` uses it once, as `if (linear && i > activeStep) return`, to refuse a jump ahead. Nothing about the drawing changes.

components.name: Display/AtlAvatarGroup
components.description:
Stacked avatar group with overflow indicator. Maps to AtlAvatarGroupSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: representing a small set of users (a team, collaborators on a doc, attendees) where individual identity matters less than the count. For a single user use Display/AtlAvatar.

Don't use when: each user needs to be addressable (use a list of Display/AtlAvatar) or the group has more than ~7 members worth showing (use a count + link).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `size`: xs | sm | md | lg | xl → AtlAvatarGroupSpec.size — mirrors AtlAvatar's size axis
- Text `max`: maximum visible avatars before overflow (default "3") → AtlAvatarGroupSpec.max

Visual: HORIZONTAL auto-layout with negative item spacing for overlap. The trailing "+N" frame is the overflow indicator. Item spacing scales with size (-6 at xs through -12 at xl).

A11y: wrap in a list with aria-label naming the group ("Team members"). Each avatar's accessible name should be the user's name; the overflow indicator should have aria-label like "and 2 more".

Status: 2026-04-27 — promoted from standalone Component to Component Set with `size` Variant axis matching AtlAvatarGroupSpec.size. 5 variants total (xs/sm/md/lg/xl).

components.name: AI/AtlChat
components.description:
Conversational AI surface. Maps to AtlChatSpec in libs/spec.

Use when: a model-driven interaction needs a UI surface. Pick the variant by attention demand: `drawer` for a side panel that coexists with the page, `popup` for a transient floating bubble, `inline` for embedded chat that lives in the page flow.

Don't use when: the user is filling a structured form (use Form/* components) or initiating a single action (use Action/AtlButton).

API surface (Figma → spec):
- Variant `variant`: drawer | popup | inline → AtlChatSpec.variant
- Boolean `open` → AtlChatSpec.open
- (code-only: `status: idle | streaming | error`, message handling)

A11y: ARIA dialog (drawer/popup) or region (inline). aria-live="polite" on the message log so streamed assistant tokens announce as they arrive. Status changes (streaming → idle/error) announced via aria-live region.

Status: 2026-04-27 — merged from three separate Sections (AtlChat / drawer, AtlChat / popup, AtlChat / inline) into one Component Set with `variant` Variant Property matching AtlChatSpec. Old `status` (idle/streaming/error) and `empty` mockup frames remain illustrated as sibling frames in the AI section pending follow-up Variant axis.

Glyph kept deliberately (2026-08-27, ADR-0058). check:figma reads this line:
- Glyph `–` on `min-icon`: this is not an icon standing in for a drawing — it is a minimise control the COMPONENT DOES NOT HAVE. AtlChatSpec exposes `open` and `onOpenChange` and nothing else; there is no minimise prop, no `is-minimised` class and no CSS for one. The master is drawing an affordance the code has never implemented. Replacing the character with an icon would make a phantom control look official; removing it would silently drop a design intent nobody has decided on. It stays, marked, until someone decides whether AtlChat gains a minimise state or the master loses the button.

Declared Boolean properties that reference no layer (2026-08-27, ADR-0058):
- Boolean `open`: declared but unbound — and it cannot be bound as the master stands. `open` reveals the whole panel: `atl-chat.tsx` renders the header, the message list and the input inside `{open && (…)}`. In Figma a Boolean toggles ONE layer's visibility, and here the panel is a background rectangle with its title, close button and messages as siblings — binding the rectangle alone would hide the panel and leave its contents floating. Group the panel and its contents into one frame, then bind that frame. Tried and reverted rather than left half-bound. Note that the popup variant keeps its bubble when closed, so the group must exclude it.

components.name: Navigation/AtlMenuItem
components.description:
The row inside AtlMenu. Maps to AtlMenuItemSpec.

Axis `state`: default | hover. `:hover` and `:focus-visible` paint the SAME background (`--ui-color-surface-sunken`), so focus is not a third drawing (ADR-0046).

- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlMenuItemSpec.disabled — `.is-disabled` sets `opacity: var(--ui-opacity-disabled)`, drawn as a surface overlay at the complement.

Geometry: `.atl-menu-item` is a row-sm (40px) that CENTRES — `padding-block: 0`, `padding-inline: var(--ui-spacing-4)`, `gap: var(--ui-spacing-3)`, leading stated tight (ADR-0052). The font size comes from `.atl-menu` (`--ui-font-size-md`); `.variant-compact` belongs to AtlMenu, not to the item.

components.name: Navigation/AtlMenuSeparator
components.description:
The 1px rule between groups inside AtlMenu. It has NO spec interface, by design: `AtlMenuSeparator()` takes no props and renders `<hr class="atl-menu-separator">`.

A part earns a master by being independently PLACEABLE, not only by having state — the refinement ADR-0056's criterion needed.

Geometry: 1px in `--ui-color-border` with `var(--ui-spacing-2)` above and below, so the master is 17px tall and stacks correctly between items.

components.name: Navigation/AtlBreadcrumbItem
components.description:
One crumb inside AtlBreadcrumbs. Maps to AtlBreadcrumbItemSpec.

Axis `current`: false | true. `current` recolours the label (`--ui-color-text`, semibold) AND removes the separator (`.is-current::after { display: none }`), so it cannot be a Boolean — a Boolean binds only to visibility.

- Glyph `›` on `separator-glyph`: the component draws the separator as CSS `content: var(--atl-separator, '›')` on `.atl-breadcrumb-item::after`. A CSS pseudo-element cannot hold an icon instance, so the master matches what the code renders today; moving it to an AtlIcon is a code change tracked in tasks/todo.md.
- `href` is not visual: it swaps the element from `<span>` to `<a>` and changes nothing drawn.

Geometry: the link carries `padding: var(--ui-spacing-1) var(--ui-spacing-2)` and `--ui-radius-sm`; the separator sits at `margin: 0 var(--ui-spacing-2)`; the list gap is 0.

components.name: Navigation/AtlTab
components.description:
One tab inside AtlTabGroup. Maps to AtlTabSpec.

Axis `state`: default | active. `.is-active` recolours the label to `--ui-color-primary` and paints the 3px bottom indicator, inset `var(--ui-spacing-2)` on each side.

- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlTabSpec.disabled — this is the flag AtlTabGroup used to declare at group level, where AtlTabGroupSpec has no such field (ADR-0061).
- Text `label`: maps to AtlTabSpec.label

Geometry: `.atl-tab-group .tablist button` DERIVES its block padding from `--ui-control-height-md` (ADR-0041). A 40px min-height box that centres its line is the same measurement without a raw 11.25px, which no token could bind. Top corners `--ui-radius-md`, bottom square.

components.name: Navigation/AtlStep
components.description:
One step inside AtlStepper. Maps to AtlStepSpec.

Axis `state`: default | active | completed | error. Each recolours the circle's border, fill and number and the label, so none of them can be a Boolean.

- Boolean `description`: maps to AtlStepSpec.description — the second line appears when the string is passed.
- Boolean `optional`: maps to AtlStepSpec.optional — adds the italic line.
- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlStepSpec.disabled — `.is-disabled` dims circle and label with `--ui-opacity-disabled`.
- Text `label`: maps to AtlStepSpec.label. `description` stays a BOOLEAN: Figma allows one property per NAME, so presence and content cannot both be called `description` — it appends a digit instead of refusing (ADR-0067), and presence is the state worth switching.
- `label` is content, not state.

Geometry: `.step-circle` is 36x36 with a 2px border and a full radius; `.step-text` sits `var(--ui-spacing-2)` below. The 2px gap between label, description and optional is a raw literal in the CSS — see tasks/todo.md.

components.name: Form/AtlOption
components.description:
One row inside AtlSelect's list. Maps to AtlOptionSpec.

DIVERGENCE, stated rather than hidden: only Angular renders this row. React and Vue emit a native `<select>`, where the operating system draws the list and no option element exists to style (ADR-0028).

Axis `state`: default | hover | active | selected. hover paints `--ui-color-surface-sunken`; active paints `--ui-color-primary-light` and recolours the text; selected only changes the weight to semibold.

- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlOptionSpec.disabled.
- `optionValue` is data, not state.

Geometry: a row-sm (40px) that centres — `padding-block: 0`, `padding-inline: var(--ui-spacing-4)`, `justify-content: space-between`, `--ui-font-size-md`.

components.name: Feedback/AtlAccordionItem
components.description:
One item inside AtlAccordionGroup. Maps to AtlAccordionItemSpec.

Axis `expanded`: false | true. `expanded` reveals the panel AND rotates the chevron 180 degrees, so a Boolean (visibility only) cannot express it.

- Boolean `disabled`: maps to AtlAccordionItemSpec.disabled — `.accordion-trigger.is-disabled` dims with `--ui-opacity-disabled`.
- `headingLevel` is not visual: it chooses h2..h6 for the trigger's wrapper and changes nothing drawn.

Geometry: `.accordion-trigger` is a row-LG (56px) that centres — `padding-block: 0`, `padding-inline: var(--ui-spacing-5)`, `gap: var(--ui-spacing-3)`, 16px semibold. The panel pads `0 var(--ui-spacing-5) var(--ui-spacing-5)`. The item's own border comes from the GROUP's variant, not from here.

components.name: AI/AtlChatMessage
components.description:
One bubble inside AtlChat. Maps to AtlChatMessageSpec.

Axis `role`: assistant | user | system, from AtlChatMessageRole. Each recolours the bubble: assistant and system take `--ui-color-surface-sunken`, user takes `--ui-color-primary` with `--ui-color-text-on-primary`, system adds italic and `--ui-color-text-muted`.

- Boolean `failed`: maps to AtlChatMessageSpec.failed — `.is-failed` ADDS a 1px dashed `--ui-color-danger` border, drawn as `_failed-border`.
- Text `content`: maps to AtlChatMessageSpec.content
- `id` and `content` are data, not state.

Geometry: `padding: var(--ui-spacing-3) var(--ui-spacing-4)`, `--ui-radius-lg`, `--ui-font-size-sm` at normal leading, `max-width: 85%` of the message list.

components.name: AI/AtlChatSuggestion
components.description:
One suggestion chip inside AtlChat. Maps to AtlChatSuggestionSpec.

No axes: the chip has one appearance. `:hover` only shifts background and border colour.

- Boolean `hint`: maps to AtlChatSuggestionSpec.hint — the second line appears when the string is passed.
- Text `label`: maps to AtlChatSuggestionSpec.label. `hint` stays a BOOLEAN for the same reason as AtlStep's `description`.
- `id` and `label` are data, not state.

Geometry: a column with `gap: var(--ui-spacing-1)`, `padding: var(--ui-spacing-3) var(--ui-spacing-4)`, `--ui-color-surface` behind a 1px `--ui-color-border`, `--ui-radius-lg`.

components.name: AI/AtlChatTyping
components.description:
The typing indicator inside AtlChat. It has NO spec interface, by design: the component takes no props and renders three animated dots plus a screen-reader label.

Placeable, not switchable — the same criterion as AtlMenuSeparator.

- `.is-inline` is a code-level variation (no padding, no background, 4px dots) that no spec field selects, so it is not an axis here.

Geometry: `gap: var(--ui-spacing-1)`, `padding: var(--ui-spacing-2) var(--ui-spacing-3)`, `--ui-color-surface-sunken`, `--ui-radius-lg`; dots are 0.375rem at 0.6 opacity. The animation does not transfer — Figma has no equivalent for `@keyframes`.

components.name: Display/AtlTh
components.description:
A header cell inside AtlTable. Maps to AtlThSpec.

Axis `sortDirection`: none | asc | desc, from `AtlSortDirection = 'asc' | 'desc' | null`. `none` is the union's `null` — a variant value cannot be null, and "unsorted" is what null means. `th.is-sorted` recolours the arrow group to `--ui-color-primary`; the inactive arrow sits at `opacity: 0.25`.

- Boolean `sortable`: maps to AtlThSpec.sortable — it ADDS the sort affordance (`.atl-th-sort-btn` wrapping `.atl-th-sort-icon`, two 10×8 arrows).
- `align`: not modelled — `AtlTableAlign` changes only `text-align`, and an axis for it would multiply this master's matrix by three for one property. It is modelled on AtlTd, where it is the cell's only state.
- `width` is content, not state.

Geometry: this draws the **md** step, which is AtlTable's default — `size` belongs to the table, not the cell. `height: var(--ui-row-height-md)` (48, a row that CENTRES), `padding-block: 0`, `padding-inline: var(--ui-spacing-4)`, leading stated tight, 14px semibold uppercase at `--ui-letter-spacing-wide` in `--ui-color-text-muted`, and a **2px** bottom rule (`--ui-border-width-thick`) where AtlTd has 1px.

components.name: Display/AtlTd
components.description:
A body cell inside AtlTable. Maps to AtlTdSpec.

Axis `align`: start | center | end, from `AtlTableAlign`. It is this master's only state, which is why the axis lives here rather than on AtlTh.

Geometry: the **md** step (AtlTable's default; `size` belongs to the table).
`height: var(--ui-row-height-md)` (48), `padding-block: 0`,
`padding-inline: var(--ui-spacing-4)`, leading stated tight, 14px, 1px bottom rule.

components.name: Display/AtlTr
components.description:
A body row inside AtlTable. Maps to AtlTrSpec.

Axis `selected`: false | true. `.is-selected` recolours the **cells**
(`--ui-color-primary-light`), not the row — the row itself paints nothing — so a
visibility Boolean cannot express it.

- Boolean `selectable`: maps to AtlTrSpec.selectable — it ADDS `.atl-tr-select-cell` (2.75rem wide, centred, holding an AtlCheckbox).
- `rowId` is data, not state.

COMPOSED: the cells are **instances of AtlTd**, so their height, padding and rule follow
that master and cannot drift from it. This is the pattern the other parents want and
mostly cannot have yet — a cell carries only text, so no content slot is needed.

components.name: Display/AtlTbody
components.description:
The body of an AtlTable. Maps to AtlTbodySpec.

No axes: a tbody has no visual state of its own.

- Boolean `empty`: maps to AtlTbodySpec.empty — it ADDS `.atl-tbody-empty-cell`
  (`padding: var(--ui-spacing-12) var(--ui-spacing-4)`, centred, 16px in
  `--ui-color-text-muted`). The sample rows stay visible behind it in Figma, where the
  code replaces them; a Boolean cannot hide siblings it does not own.
- `colSpan` is data, not state.

COMPOSED: the rows are **instances of AtlTr**, which are themselves composed of AtlTd.
